newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: Benco, BHP unit in 110 mln rand deal.
newsitem.headline: Benco, BHP unit in 110 mln rand deal.

text.p: Marine diamond exploration and mining company Benguela Concessions Ltd said on Monday it would acquire all the sea diamond mining concessions belonging to its joint-venture partner BHP Minerals International Exploration Inc in a deal worth 110 million rand.

The deal will give BHP a 25 percent stake in Benco, while Benco will acquire BHP's entire interest in the existing joint venture, including Diamond Fields International shares, all equipment and a vast data base of exploration results.
The joint venture was formed in January 1993 to explore and develop marine diamond mining deposits off the west coast of South Africa.
"This is a fantastic show of faith in Benco by one of the world's largest mining companies," Benco chairman John Gurney said in a statement on Monday.
"Whilst Benco has funded the joint venture operations since late 1995, it is gratifying to know that BHP will continue their interests through Benco."
The changes, which have to be approved by shareholders, will give Benco outright control over sea concessions 2(b), 3(b), 5(b), 6(a) and (b), 13(c) and 18(d).
Further involvement with joint venture partner Ocean Diamond Mining includes concessions 6(c) and 14(c).
Benco currently operates a mining vessel, Moonstar, in concessions 2(b) and 3(b) for its joint venture with Moonstone Diamond Corporation.
Gurney said that the deal would not have any significant impact on Benco's earnings in the medium term.
